question.problem:
Suppose that $f(x)$ is defined as

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡x, & x\le 0 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡x, & x>0.\end{aligned}
$$

On which of the following intervals can the extreme value theorem be applied to the function?

I. $[-2,-1]$

II. $[-1,1]$

III. $(0,1]$
question.worked_solution:
Remember that the extreme value theorem is only applicable to closed intervals on which the function is continuous.

So, let's check whether the function is continuous on each of the intervals.

- First, consider $[-2,-1].$ In this interval, $f(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and so $f(x)$ is continuous on $[-2,-1].$  Therefore, the extreme value theorem is applicable on this interval.

- Now, consider the interval $[-1,1].$ In this case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)=-\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $f(x)$ has an essential discontinuity at $x=0.$ Therefore, $f(x)$ is not continuous on the interval $[-1,1],$ and the extreme value theorem is not applicable on this interval.

- Finally, we note that the interval $(0,1]$ is not closed, so the extreme value theorem is not applicable.

In conclusion, the correct answer is "I only".
